Python has always been known as a flexible and beginner friendly language. One reason for this is that Python does not force you to declare types. You can write code quickly and focus on logic instead of rules.
But as projects grow, this flexibility can turn into confusion. It becomes harder to know what kind of data a function expects or returns. This is where type hints come in.
Type hints are now widely used in modern Python codebases. They are not required, but they are strongly recommended.
What Are Type Hints
Type hints let you describe what type of data a variable or function should work with.
They do not change how Python runs your code. Python still behaves the same way at runtime. Type hints exist to help humans and tools understand your code better.

Heaps are a fundamental data structure in computer science, commonly used to implement priority queues and optimize algorithms. In this blog post, we will delve into the world of heaps, exploring their structure, operations, and applications.
A heap is a specialized tree-based data structure that satisfies the heap property. There are two main types of heaps: min-heap and max-heap. In a min-heap, the parent node is smaller than or equal to its children, while in a max-heap, the parent node is larger than or equal to its children.
To insert an element into a heap, we first place the element at the bottom level of the heap, maintaining the heap property. We then compare the element with its parent and swap if necessary until the heap property is restored.
